subject: FinLytics production 429s and latency — suspected rate-limit / quota misconfiguration
messages:
From: Katie Brooks <katie.brooks@finlytics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-15T08:02:14-08:00
Subject: Production: spike in latency + 429s (region us-west)

Jonas —

We started seeing elevated latencies and a surge of 429 responses across several of our production routes around 07:50 PT. This is affecting our real-time scoring pipeline and causing downstream backpressure.

Key symptoms:
- Intermittent 429s returned from Redwood endpoint (approx 15-25% of requests during window)
- Median p95 latency jumped from ~150ms to 1.2s
- No recent changes on our side; feature flags unchanged

We escalated to on-call but wanted to loop you directly. Can you confirm if this is on Redwood's side and whether there is a mitigation we should apply? Our SREs are standing by.

Attachments: small client-side trace sent to ops@finlytics.com

Thanks,
Katie Brooks
Head of Engineering, FinLytics

Thanks for the heads-up and the trace. I'm pulling logs now and have engaged our infra on-call. A few quick asks that will help:

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-15T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: URGENT: FinLytics production 429/latency — initial findings + logs attached

Team —

Summary: FinLytics reported a production incident (see Katie's note below). I collected initial logs and a short snippet is attached (redwood_logs_20261215_snippet.txt). High-level observations:
- Spike in 429s correlates with a burst of requests starting ~07:50 PT from FinLytics; requests then throttled across multiple routes.
- Error rates elevated at the gateway layer and the per-tenant token-bucket counter shows a sudden refill/consumption pattern inconsistent with normal behavior.
- p95 latency increase appears after the 429s start — likely retries/backoff.

Hypothesis: misconfiguration of quota/burst policy for this account (or a regression in burst window calculation) caused an aggressive enforcement that applied globally rather than per-route, resulting in broad throttling.

Immediate asks:
1) Rishi — can infra quickly validate token-bucket params and whether the recent policy deploy (2026-12-15 07:30 PT) changed units (per-account vs per-route)? If so, rollback or hotfix.
2) Laura — please prepare the customer-facing status note and a remediation timeline (15/60/240 min options).
3) Marissa/Evelyn — recommend we pre-approve a small goodwill credit for FinLytics while we clear root cause (estimate ready once Rishi confirms impact).

Attachments: redwood_logs_20261215_snippet.txt (log excerpt), sla_latency_report_Q4.pdf (background)

Jonas
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-15T09:10:05-08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: FinLytics production 429/latency — initial findings + logs attached

Quick update from infra dive:
- We confirmed a deployment at 07:31 PT that updated the burst policy codepath (hotfix for multi-tenant burst accounting). The intent was to scope burst buckets per-route; due to a config flag flip a migration job defaulted the granularity to "account-global" for tenants that had an older quota schema.
- Result: for tenants like FinLytics that have high parallelism, the global bucket hit its threshold quickly and the gateway started returning 429s for unrelated routes.
- The token-bucket refill rate was correct but the capacity calculation used an incorrect multiplier (x0.1) under the new flag for some accounts — effectively lowering allowed burst capacity by 90%.

Action taken:
- Rolled the config change back at 08:58 PT for affected tenants (including FinLytics).
- Added a temporary emergency override to raise bucket capacity for FinLytics to pre-incident baseline.
- Root cause flagged: migration default + incomplete migration testing matrix for older quota schemas.

Next steps (by priority):
- Permanent fix to migration and a Canary validation job (owner: infra, ETA: 48h).
- Post-incident runbook update and alerting (owner: platform reliability, ETA: 72h).
- Customer remediation plan and credit recommendation (owner: accounts/finance).

Logs and timeline attached. We'll need comms asap.

— Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-15T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Customer comms + exec summary for FinLytics incident

Team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Rishi, thanks for confirming root cause and rollback. Summary for execs and CS:
- Impact: FinLytics experienced elevated 429s and latency from 07:50–08:58 PT; rollback restored normal behavior. Estimated request loss window ~68 minutes.
- Root cause: burst/quota migration defaulted to account-global with an erroneous capacity multiplier.
- Remediation done: rollback + emergency override at 08:58 PT. Permanent fix planned with 48–72h timeline.
- Customer ask: FinLytics requests a detailed post-mortem and a goodwill credit for the incident.

Proposed immediate customer message (short):
"Katie — we identified a rate-limit configuration regression that caused broader-than-intended throttling on 2026-12-15. We rolled back the change and restored normal service; we're conducting a full post-mortem and will share a timeline for permanent fixes. Our team will follow up with proposed credits and next steps by EOD tomorrow."

Please confirm approval for up to a 10% monthly credit for this customer while we finalize the impact analysis. If approved I will send the note and schedule a joint A/C call.

Marissa
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
